newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk policemen face jail for journalist's death.
newsitem.headline: Turk policemen face jail for journalist's death.

text.p: Prosecutors on Thursday demanded sentences between three and 15 years for 48 Turkish policemen charged with the beating to death of a leftist journalist, Anatolian news agency said.
The trial of the policemen restarted in the western town of Afyon on Thursday, over a year after the death of Metin Goktepe.
Goktepe was allegedly battered to death by police last January. He was among scores of people rounded up at random for an identity check after the funerals of two far-left jail inmates.
The court prosecutors demanded 15 year jail sentences for 11 of the policemen -- charged with manslaughter -- who were allegedly directly involved with beating Goktepe to death.
They asked for sentences of three years for 37 other policemen for "dereliction of duty".

Anatolian said that none of the 48 policemen were at the hearing held in a sport centre in the western town of Afyon. The hearing was attended by up to 2,000 people, including journalists and leftist party MPs.

The case has been delayed after being transferred twice to different provinces for what officials describe as security concerns. But rights activists said the moves were part of an attempt to keep the proceedings out of the public eye by dragging out the trial.

Turkey has come under criticism from its Western allies over its shaky human rights record. Allegations of abuse include extrajudical killing, torture in police custody, restrictions on expression and the army's fight against Kurdish rebels in the southeast.
The United States said in its annual report on human rights that Turkey still had grave human rights problems last year and that the situation had gone downhill in some ways.
